import re
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

def new_doc(font='Times New Roman', size=11.5):
    d = Document()
    st = d.styles['Normal']
    st.font.name = font
    st.font.size = Pt(size)
    st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), font)
    st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    st.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.08
    for s in ['Heading 1','Heading 2','Heading 3']:
        hs = d.styles[s]
        hs.font.name = font
        hs.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), font)
        hs.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0,0,0)
        hs.font.bold = True
    d.styles['Heading 1'].font.size = Pt(13)
    d.styles['Heading 2'].font.size = Pt(12)
    d.styles['Heading 3'].font.size = Pt(11.5)
    for sec in d.sections:
        sec.left_margin = sec.right_margin = Inches(1)
        sec.top_margin = sec.bottom_margin = Inches(1)
    return d

TOK = re.compile(r'(\*\*.+?\*\*|\*.+?\*|__.+?__)')
def add_runs(p, text, size=None, color=None):
    for part in TOK.split(text):
        if not part:
            continue
        if part.startswith('**') and part.endswith('**'):
            r = p.add_run(part[2:-2]); r.bold = True
        elif part.startswith('__') and part.endswith('__'):
            r = p.add_run(part[2:-2]); r.underline = True
        elif part.startswith('*') and part.endswith('*') and len(part) > 2:
            r = p.add_run(part[1:-1]); r.italic = True
        else:
            r = p.add_run(part)
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if color: r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(*color)
    return p

def para(d, text, indent=0.0, first=0.0, align=None, size=None, after=None, before=None, keep=False, color=None):
    p = d.add_paragraph()
    add_runs(p, text, size=size, color=color)
    pf = p.paragraph_format
    if indent: pf.left_indent = Inches(indent)
    if first: pf.first_line_indent = Inches(first)
    if align == 'center': p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    elif align == 'right': p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
    elif align == 'justify': p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    if after is not None: pf.space_after = Pt(after)
    if before is not None: pf.space_before = Pt(before)
    if keep: pf.keep_with_next = True
    return p

def head(d, text, level=1):
    h = d.add_heading(level=level)
    add_runs(h, text)
    return h

def bullet(d, text, level=0):
    p = d.add_paragraph(style='List Bullet' if level == 0 else 'List Bullet 2')
    add_runs(p, text)
    return p

def shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement('w:shd')
    shd.set(qn('w:val'), 'clear'); shd.set(qn('w:color'), 'auto'); shd.set(qn('w:fill'), hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(shd)

def table(d, header, rows, widths=None, size=9, header_fill='D9D9D9'):
    t = d.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(header))
    t.style = 'Table Grid'
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i, h in enumerate(header):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]
        c.text = ''
        add_runs(c.paragraphs[0], '**' + h + '**', size=size)
        shade(c, header_fill)
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i, val in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ''
            lines = str(val).split('\n')
            add_runs(cells[i].paragraphs[0], lines[0], size=size)
            for ln in lines[1:]:
                add_runs(cells[i].add_paragraph(), ln, size=size)
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    # repeat header
    trPr = t.rows[0]._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    th = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); th.set(qn('w:val'), 'true'); trPr.append(th)
    d.add_paragraph()
    return t

def footer_text(d, text):
    for sec in d.sections:
        p = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = ''
        add_runs(p, text, size=8)
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER

def header_text(d, text):
    for sec in d.sections:
        p = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = ''
        add_runs(p, text, size=8, color=(0xA0,0,0))
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT

Engelman” in the Security Agreement. “Cromdale Consulting” is also the name of the securities intermediary in Schedule V, which suggests a document-assembly error.",

issue("B-7","Organizational documents — excerpts only; certification defects","H",

head(d, "D. Collateral, Perfection and Priority", 2)
issue("D-1","Ironbridge all-assets UCC-1 not terminated; prior facility facts inconsistent","G",
 "Delaware File No. 2019-4572810 (filed August 9, 2019; continued July 22, 2024 to August 9, 2029) covers all of the Borrower’s assets. No UCC-3 termination was of record on June 8, 2025. The Credit Agreement dates the Prior Credit Facility March 15, 2019. Terracotta Schedule 5.11 (April 2021) shows Ironbridge as a $100 million facility maturing August 9, 2024. The Officer’s Certificate shows $118.75 million outstanding in 2025.",
 "Ironbridge’s earlier filing would prime the Agent under UCC Section 9-322(a)(1) while it secures obligations. Section 4.01(g) is unsatisfied, and opinion 7(g) is bracketed.",
 "Obtain the Ironbridge payoff letter (amount, per diem, automatic lien release, authorization for the Borrower or Agent to file the UCC-3, and return of possessory collateral). File the UCC-3 at funding and obtain filed-stamped evidence. Reconcile the facility size and maturity (extension or upsizing amendments).")
issue("D-2","Unreleased $347,218.64 Ohio state tax lien against the Borrower","G",
 "Ohio Secretary of State notice OH-2024-TL-0048271 (March 3, 2024) covers all property for taxes, penalties and interest under ORC Chapters 5739 and 5747. It does not appear on Schedule 7.02. It contradicts Credit Agreement Section 5.08 (no tax liens filed) and is likely not a Permitted Lien: clause (i) covers only taxes not yet delinquent or contested in good faith with reserves. The Search Report itself has reliability problems. It names the claimant as a “Great Lakes Tax Authority, Ohio Department of Revenue” (Ohio’s agency is the Department of Taxation). It describes Chapter 5739 as the commercial activity tax (Chapter 5739 is sales and use tax; the CAT is Chapter 5751). And Ohio tax liens are typically recorded as judgment liens with the county clerk of courts, which were not searched. The Search Report also cites the wrong Credit Agreement sections (5.08/5.09 rather than 5.07/5.08).",
 "A statutory tax lien may prime the Agent regardless of filing priority, so we give no priority opinion over it (Annex G, Part 2). The Officer’s Certificate representations are inaccurate.",
 "Obtain a certified copy of the lien notice and confirm the claimant and the underlying assessment. Pay the lien and file a release before closing (fund from proceeds with a release in escrow if necessary). If it is contested, add it to Schedule 7.02 with reserves and disclose it. Correct Section 5.08 and the Officer’s Certificate. Run Summit County (and other county) judgment and tax-lien searches.")
issue("D-3","Aldersgate filing — true lease or security interest?","M",
 "The Search Report treats Aldersgate as a precautionary true-lease filing. Credit Agreement Schedule 7.01 lists it as “Capital Lease Obligations … Secured by leased equipment” (about $4.8 million). The Officer’s Certificate identifies the Aldersgate Master Lease as a PFT agreement, while Schedule 5.04 and the UCC filing name the Borrower. Terracotta Schedule 5.11 (April 2021) lists Aldersgate obligations that predate the February 1, 2022 Master Lease.",
 "If the lease is a disguised security interest under UCC Section 1-203, Aldersgate has a prior perfected lien in the described equipment. It is a Permitted Lien, but it counts toward the Terracotta cap (Issue A-1). The draft excepts it in Annex G.",
 "Obtain the Master Lease and schedules. Determine its characterization and the correct obligor, and conform Schedules 5.04 and 7.01 and the Officer’s Certificate.")
issue("D-4","Pledged share counts in Security Agreement Schedule I do not match issuers’ capitalization","H",
 "Schedule I lists PFT Certificate C-2001 for 1,000,000 shares and PAC Certificate C-3001 for 500,000 shares. PFT’s Articles and PAC’s Certificate of Incorporation each authorize, and show outstanding, 1,000 shares. The Borrower’s 4,500,000 shares (C-1001) are consistent.",
 "Either the certificates describe shares that were never validly issued (an over-issue problem under Article 8) or the schedule is wrong. Opinion 7(e) cannot be given until we inspect the original certificates and stock ledgers.",
 "Inspect certificates C-1001, C-2001 and C-3001 and the stock ledgers. Correct Schedule I, and the Pledge Agreement schedule if separate. Deliver the original certificates with stock powers executed in blank, and agree where the Agent will hold them (the governing law for control follows the certificate’s location).")
issue("D-5","Deposit and securities account control agreements not furnished; intermediary identity","H",
 "Security Agreement Schedule V lists 10 accounts. Three are at Ridgeline itself, where control is automatic under Section 9-104(a)(1). Five DACAs are with third-party banks (First Saxonbrook, Great Lakes Commercial Bank (two accounts), Citizens National Bank (Elkhart, IN) and Heartland Bank of Kansas). Two SACAs are with “Cromdale Consulting Wealth Advisors”. None has been furnished. Security Agreement Sections 3.08(b)–(c) and 6.02(c) state that control “has been granted”. Drummond’s letter expressly requires the opinion to address the DACAs and SACAs.",
 "Opinions 7(c) and 7(d) are bracketed. The bank’s jurisdiction (Section 9-304) and intermediary’s jurisdiction (Section 8-110(e)) may be Indiana, Kansas or elsewhere, outside our covered law. A consulting or advisory firm may not be a “securities intermediary” under Section 8-102(a)(14), in which case Section 8-106(d) control would be unavailable.",
 "Obtain the executed DACAs and SACAs. Confirm each one’s governing-law and jurisdiction clause and Cromdale’s status (broker-dealer or bank custodian). If a jurisdiction falls outside our coverage, either have the agreement select New York, Delaware or Ohio as the bank’s or intermediary’s jurisdiction or obtain local counsel.")
issue("D-6","Intellectual property schedules irreconcilable; IP filings not prepared; registered copyrights","H",
 "Credit Agreement Schedule 5.15 lists owned patents 8,765,432 (PFT), 9,123,456 (Borrower) and 10,456,789 (PAC), and trademarks PINNACLE (Reg. No. 4,567,890), PINNACLE FASTENER TECHNOLOGIES, PINNACLE AEROSPACE and DURASHIELD. Security Agreement Schedule IV lists entirely different patents (9,812,445; 10,234,678; 10,567,890; 11,012,334 owned by PCSS; Application 17/345,221) and marks (PINNACLE Reg. No. 4,215,887; PINNACLE & Design; TORQLOCK; DURABOND; AEROFORM), plus two registered copyrights. No USPTO or Copyright Office searches were run (Search Report Section 7.5), and no short-form IP security agreements exist for recordation (Security Agreement Section 6.03).",
 "UCC filing perfects security interests in patents and trademarks, but recordation with the USPTO matters as against subsequent assignees. A security interest in **registered** copyrights is generally perfected only by recording with the Copyright Office (*In re Peregrine Entertainment, Ltd.*, 116 B.R. 194 (C.D. Cal. 1990); *In re World Auxiliary Power Co.*, 303 F.3d 1120 (9th Cir. 2002)). The draft excludes registered copyrights from opinion 7(f).",
 "Run USPTO assignment and Copyright Office searches. Reconcile the schedules with the client. Prepare and record patent, trademark and copyright security agreements at closing.")
issue("D-7","Security Agreement Schedule III and related data errors","M",
 "Schedule III organizational IDs conflict with the other records (Issue C-4). Addresses differ: PFT at Youngstown, OH; PCSS at Elkhart, IN; PAC at Wichita, KS. Elsewhere these are Akron suites 300, 340, 350 and 360 or the Schedule 5.17 sites. The Ohio statutory agent is shown as “DC Statutory Agent System”, but PFT’s Articles name Okonkwo. The representation in Section 3.06 is that Schedule III is “true, complete, and correct in all respects”.",
 "Perfection against registered organizations turns on the state of organization, so the filings are not defective. The representations are inaccurate, however, and federal tax lien searches must be run where each corporation’s principal executive office is located (IRC Section 6323(f)).",
 "Correct Schedule III and run federal tax lien searches in the correct principal-office state for each Opinion Party.")
issue("D-8","Search Report gaps and internal inconsistencies","H",
 "Searches cover only the Delaware and Ohio Secretaries of State. Ohio searches were run only against the Borrower and PFT, although Section 4.01(f)(ii) requires UCC, tax-lien **and judgment** searches for **each** Loan Party in its jurisdiction of organization **and Ohio**. No judgment, county fixture, USPTO or Copyright Office searches were run. The report is “current through June 8, 2025” yet reflects UCC-1s filed June 10, 2025. Certified search certificates are “maintained in our files” but have not been reviewed.",
 "Section 4.01(f) is not satisfied, and priority opinion 7(g) rests on an incomplete and internally inconsistent report.",
 "Order Ohio UCC, tax-lien and judgment searches for the Parent Guarantor, PCSS and PAC, plus county judgment searches. Order a bring-down Delaware and Ohio search after the Ironbridge UCC-3 and the new filings index. Review the National Lien Search Services certificates.")
issue("D-9","Pledge Agreement and Guaranty Agreement not furnished; party descriptions inconsistent","H",
 "The Credit Agreement describes the Pledge Agreement as “among the Loan Parties” and pledging 100% of each Subsidiary Guarantor’s equity. Drummond describes it as among the Borrower, the Parent Guarantor and the Agent. Security Agreement Section 2.02 already pledges the same equity, plus the Borrower’s stock. The Guaranty is Article X of the Credit Agreement, but Drummond’s letter, the Security Agreement recitals and the guarantor consents refer to a separate Guaranty or Subsidiary Guaranty, which Section 1.01 of the Credit Agreement does not define.",
 "We cannot opine on unseen documents. The guarantor consents may not cover the Credit Agreement joinder itself if no separate guaranty is executed.",
 "Obtain final forms. Conform the party lists and definitions. Make sure each new consent names the Credit Agreement (Article X) and any separate guaranty.")
issue("D-10","Pre-closing UCC-1 filings and commercial tort claim schedule","L",
 "UCC-1s were filed June 10, 2025, before the Security Agreement was authenticated. Security Agreement Schedule II describes the Borrower’s Morrison counterclaims as commercial tort claims, but those counterclaims are for unpaid invoices, which are contract claims (accounts or general intangibles).",
 "A pre-filing is effective if the debtor authorized it in an authenticated record (Section 9-509), and authentication of the Security Agreement ratifies it under Section 9-509(b). Schedule II is harmless but inaccurate.",
 "Obtain pre-filing authorization letters (or rely on the Section 9-509(b) ratification) and correct Schedule II.")
issue("D-11","Security Agreement and Credit Agreement drafting errors","M",
 "Security Agreement Section 7.03 cites “Section 10.02” of the Credit Agreement for notices (the notice section is 11.01). The terms “Payment in Full”, “Permitted Dispositions” and “Subsidiary Guaranty” are used but not defined in the Credit Agreement. The Agent’s notice e-mail differs between the documents (agencyservices@ridgelinebank.com versus agencynotices@ridgelinenational.com). The Korvin license appears under “Copyright License”. Credit Agreement Section 11.01 gives Drummond’s e-mail as rdrummond@drummondlaw.com, while the letter uses @drummondassociates.com. The Security Agreement represents first-priority liens (Section 3.05(c)) despite the tax lien and the Ironbridge filing.",
 "Undefined terms and cross-reference errors bear on enforceability (opinion 4) and invite disputes.",
 "Send a conforming-changes list to Drummond.")

 "Section 3(e) and Schedule A certify that no third-party consent is required other than UCC filings, which is false because of the Korvin and Terracotta conflicts.  "Morrison: Schedule 5.06 states that W&C assessed the claim and that the Borrower answered and counterclaimed. The Officer’s Certificate attributes the assessment to Kellner & Brandt LLP and refers to a pending motion to dismiss.  "Opinion 8 discloses both matters regardless of MAE (as requested) and expresses no view on outcome. Our own role in Morrison must be confirmed because it bears on what “our knowledge” covers.",

head(d, "F. Opinion Scope and Form — Points for Lender Counsel", 2)
for t in [
 "**New York governing law.** Every Transaction Document selects New York law; Drummond’s acceptable limitations cover Ohio, Delaware and federal law and Article 9 only. The draft offers an “as if Ohio law governed” enforceability opinion (assumption (8)) plus an Ohio choice-of-law opinion (paragraph 4A; Ohio follows Restatement (Second) of Conflict of Laws Section 187, *Schulke Radio Prods., Ltd. v. Midwestern Broad. Co.*, 6 Ohio St. 3d 436 (1983)). Alternative: New York counsel delivers the enforceability opinion.",
 "**First-priority opinion.** Consistent with TriBar practice, the draft declines a general “first-priority subject only to Permitted Liens” opinion. It gives (i) a search-based filing-priority opinion with each Search Report filing specifically addressed (as the letter asks) and (ii) Article 8 protected-purchaser and Section 9-328 control priority for the certificated pledged shares.",
 "**“Where required” foreign qualification.** The draft declines this factual formulation and gives certificate-based opinions for the listed states.",
 "**Non-standard assumptions (8)–(10) and qualifications (j)–(n).** These are not on Drummond’s list. The letter asks that they be raised now; they are bracketed in the draft.",
 "**Reliance by assignees.** The draft offers bracketed reliance by future Section 11.04 assignees. Drummond’s limitation (3) would allow addressees only.",
 "**Closing date.** June 15, 2025 is a Sunday and not a Business Day; the closing and funding date must be confirmed and certificate windows re-measured.",
 "**Opinion giver’s involvement.** Ms. Engstrom attended and presented at the May 28 board meeting. Schedule 5.06 identifies W&C as having assessed Morrison. These points do not bar the opinion, but the knowledge definition and Annex H must reflect them accurately."]:
